text:
sasha: Quick thread to finalize the benchmark narrative and go/no-go checklist for launch week. Need a single headline, three clear charts, a short X post, and routing rules for inbound estimates. Who can validate numbers and provide methodology?

anya: For the headline I propose: "Cut inference cost without breaking latency guarantees." Then in the blog we include a conservative lab callout (e.g., "Lab sweep: up to ~1.5x infra savings at matched P95 for 256-token chat flows; lab pricing used").

miguel: Agree with conservative phrasing. We'll add a parenthetical "(lab sweep)" and a footnote describing pricing assumptions. Engineering to confirm.

jamal: I'll run a deterministic sweep and post CSV. Test matrix: redwood-4b-fp16, redwood-4b-q8, redwood-4b-q4; seq lengths 64/256/512; batches 1/4/16. Metrics: p50, p95, tokens/sec. Cost calc = pro-rated GPU-min + infra overhead, normalized per 100k tokens.

benchbot: Benchmark queued by jamal. Tracker: https://redwood.share/bench/launch-playbook-2024 (read-only). Results will appear in the tracker.

olivia: GTM checklist: 1) landing one-liner + 3 bullets, 2) webinar CTA collecting avg tokens/min & expected concurrency, 3) UTM tags utm_campaign=bench_launch_2024&utm_source=social, 4) SDR tag "bench_estimate" and routing rules (growth-sdr default; enterprise-sdr if tokens/min > 5k or monthly > 10M).

anya: Chart set request for design: A) P95 latency vs throughput (lines per model variant, highlight matched-P95 points), B) Cost per 100k tokens (hosted vs dedicated vs baseline), C) Tail-latency heatmap/violin. Keep labels simple and add a small methodology inset.

designbot: Noted. We'll deliver: hero chart for the blog, compact cost badge for social, and a methodology slide with the command snippet. Palette: product blues + neutral grays; P95 line emphasized. Figma link: figma.com/redwood/bench-tiles (comments enabled).

jamal: Sweep complete. Short summary: redwood-4b-q8 shows ~1.5x lower infra cost at matched P95 for seq=256 batch=4 under lab pricing (GPU $3.10/hr, infra overhead 12%). For seq=512 the improvement narrows to ~1.2x. Full CSV uploaded to tracker.

miguel: That supports the narrative. Add explicit footnotes: lab pricing, workload assumptions, and that Dedicated reserved capacity yields larger savings at sustained throughput.

anya: Draft blog opening: start with the problem (inference cost growth + unpredictable tail latency), then our approach (batching, KV cache, quantization, smart routing), then the benchmark results and methodology. Keep tech levers as short bullet points with customer-facing benefits.

olivia: Landing blurb draft: "Redwood Inference: predictable latency SLOs and lower per-token cost across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments." CTA: "Get estimate". I will add the short form fields for avg tokens/min and monthly tokens.

jamal: Repro command for methodology slide:
```bash
python tools/bench_sweep.py \
  --models redwood-4b-fp16,redwood-4b-q8,redwood-4b-q4 \
  --seq 64,256,512 \
  --batch 1,4,16 \
  --metrics p50,p95,tokens_per_sec \
  --out results/launch_playbook.csv
```

benchbot: Slide export uploaded: https://redwood.share/slides/bench-playbook-v1. Comments enabled.

anya: Social X copy suggestion: "New: benchmarked inference that balances latency SLOs with lower per-token cost. See lab results + request a personalized estimate. [link] #inference #llm" Keep under 220 chars.

miguel: We'll add an engineer quote for the blog about how batching + KV caching reduce per-token compute without increasing P95. I'll draft one after reviewing the CSV.

olivia: Routing automation: tag inbound leads with channel=benchmark, tag bench_estimate, and if avg tokens/min >5k OR monthly_tokens >10M set lead_priority=enterprise. SDRs to add notes whether lead requested dedicated estimate.

sasha: Next steps and timeline: 1) Jamal finalize methodology note and CSV (today). 2) Design to deliver three chart variants (EOD tomorrow). 3) Olivia + Anya draft blog, landing, and social (tomorrow AM). 4) Miguel review for technical accuracy (tomorrow noon). 5) Internal review + sign-off 1600PT day after. 6) Webinar dry run on launch week.

designbot: We'll attach export-ready SVGs and a compact PNG for social. Also include a slide template with the methodology snippet and footnotes.

jamal: One small caveat in the methodology: we used warm KV caches and disabled cold-start penalties. We'll add that note in the footnotes to avoid overclaiming.

anya: Good catch. Add a line: "Results assume warmed runtime state (KV cache) and no cold-start overhead."

benchbot: Final upload: methodology.md and results CSV available in tracker. Link: https://redwood.share/bench/launch-playbook-2024 (files: methodology.md, results.csv, slides.pdf).

sasha: Thanks everyone. If anyone sees a claim that feels risky, flag here. We'll keep public messaging conservative and put detailed assumptions in the methodology doc. Plan to circulate the first external drafts by EOD tomorrow. :rocket:
